# Tensile test: elastic modulus estimates

Stress was regressed on strain using ordinary least squares, pooling the measurements from all three specimens within each material. Each fit includes a free intercept; the reported modulus is the fitted slope. Strain is dimensionless, so the slope is in MPa (converted to GPa below). Fits cover the full supplied strain interval (0.0002–0.0020).

| Material | Specimens | Measurements | Modulus (GPa) | Intercept (MPa) | R² |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Aluminum | 3 | 30 | 69.38 | -0.31 | 0.9983 |
| Steel | 3 | 30 | 199.06 | 0.62 | 0.9984 |
| Titanium | 3 | 30 | 116.56 | -0.77 | 0.9979 |

The steel specimens have the highest estimated modulus, followed by titanium and aluminum. These are apparent slopes over the measured range; the data do not identify a separate elastic-only region or a forced-zero fit, so estimates may depend on the selected strain interval and the free-intercept assumption.
